title: Settings Hub hardening: per-plugin capability, real integration tests, CI and docs realignment
description: Execution state for issue #48. Read this file at the start of every session and continue from the first work item that is not completed. After every finished task or commit: flip its status, append a dated log entry to the work item, add a changelog entry when the note is cross-cutting, and bump lastUpdated. Narrative and design live in docs/settings-hub-hardening-plan.md and are not rewritten to record progress.

taskTemplate.note: Every phase runs this lifecycle around its phase-specific tasks. One phase is one branch and one PR referencing #48. Phase 1 uses the issue branch 48-settings-hub-hardening; later phases use 48-phase-<n>-<slug> created from up-to-date main with `gh issue develop 48 --base main --name <branch>`.

steps.description: Create or check out the phase branch from up-to-date main and confirm the previous phase is merged.
Complete the phase-specific tasks listed in the work item.

Run composer phpcs, composer phpstan and the unit and integration suites against a real WordPress test install (WP_TESTS_DIR set, DB wp_settings_hub_test, root with an empty password on 127.0.0.1 locally).
Run core-review --budget medium (thorough for Phase 5), apply every critical and warning finding, and re-run until nothing new is reported.
Push, open the PR referencing #48 with this JSON updated in the same PR, and get CI green.

workItems.title: Phase 1: CI and tooling
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-settings-hub-hardening (already created and linked to #48; carries this plan). Make CI fail on what it claims to check, test the supported WordPress range, and block releases with a stale PACKAGE_VERSION. Known limitation: on a manual release dispatch the reusable quality-checks job still checks out the dispatching ref, not the tag; only validate and build use the tag.
findings: quality-checks.yml runs `composer phpcbf || true` before `composer phpcs`, so fixable style violations never fail CI.

integration-guide.php fails `php -l` (unexpected token "public" on line 475): a nested docblock at :456-474 closes the outer /* */ opened at :387. It is excluded from PHPCS and PHPStan, so nothing catches it.

actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 is commented `# v5.2.2` in ci.yml, quality-checks.yml and release.yml; that SHA is tag v7.0.1 and v5.2.2 does not exist. actions/github-script@v9 in auto-merge-dependabot.yml is a floating tag (v9 = 3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3). setup-php 2.40.0, cache v6.1.0, codecov v7.1.1 and action-gh-release v3.0.3 pins are correct.
CI installs WordPress 'latest' only and starts MySQL via apt/systemctl; the reference repo silver-assist-security uses a mysql:8.0 service container, host 127.0.0.1 and a WP version matrix.

release.yml validates only that CHANGELOG.md contains the tag; PACKAGE_VERSION is still '1.2.0' at v1.2.1 and v1.2.2. The workflow_dispatch path derives VERSION from GITHUB_REF, which is refs/heads/main on a manual run.

scripts/install-wp-tests.sh is a hand copy lacking empty-password support; `[ ! -f wp-tests-config.php ]` at :130 tests the working directory. silver-assist-security wraps vendor/silverassist/wp-coding-standards/scripts/install-wp-tests.sh in 3 lines.

phpunit.xml hardcodes WP_TESTS_DIR=/tmp/wordpress-tests-lib while the install script uses $TMPDIR (/var/folders/... on macOS); WP_TESTS_PHPUNIT_POLYFILLS_PATH is relative; bootstrap hint says password 'root' and host localhost.

tasks.notes: 48-settings-hub-hardening created with gh issue develop 48.
WP 6.5 x PHP 8.2; WP latest x PHP 8.2/8.3/8.4; one WP_MULTISITE=1 job on latest.
scripts/run-quality-checks.sh: phpcbf removed from `all`, --warning-severity=0 dropped.
coverage.xml ignored; phpunit --list-tests shows 24 tests and no duplicates across the unit, integration and all suites.

log.summary: Issue #48 opened and branch 48-settings-hub-hardening created and linked. Baseline verified against a real WordPress 7.1.3 test install: unit 16/16, integration 8/8, all 24/24 (86 assertions); also 24/24 with WP_MULTISITE=1. phpcs and phpstan pass; composer audit clean.

Phase 1 implemented. quality-checks.yml: removed `composer phpcbf || true`, mysql:8.0 service container on 127.0.0.1, new wordpress-version and multisite inputs, php -l integration-guide.php, unit and integration run as separate steps, coverage collected only on the coverage job. ci.yml: added WP 6.5 and multisite jobs. release.yml: PACKAGE_VERSION must equal the tag, manual runs use the tag input (checkout ref, VERSION, tag_name). Pins: checkout comments corrected to v7.0.1, github-script pinned to its v9 SHA. integration-guide.php: nested docblock turned into // comments (php -l passes). scripts/install-wp-tests.sh is now a wrapper over the shared script; phpunit.xml no longer hardcodes WP_TESTS_DIR or the relative polyfills path (bootstrap defines the absolute path); bootstrap hint updated.

Verified locally: unit 16/16 and integration 8/8 on WP 7.1.3 and on WP 6.5, 24/24 with WP_MULTISITE=1, run with no WP_TESTS_DIR set and from another working directory; phpcs and phpstan clean. The wrapper install into a clean TMPDIR created the suite and database on the first run. Not verifiable locally: the new workflow jobs themselves, which run on the PR.

PR #50 opened. All checks green on the first run: PHP 8.2, 8.3 and 8.4 on WP latest, WP 6.5, multisite, CodeQL and the security scan. Added the local quality script alignment and the coverage.xml ignore after the plan verification.

Merged as PR #50 (squash, admin override because the only blocker was the required review) at 10d4fa2. All 8 checks were green. The merge auto-closed #48 because the PR was linked through `gh issue develop`; the issue was reopened. Later phases use plain branches, with no development link.

workItems.title: Phase 2: Test infrastructure and real integration tests
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-2-integration-tests. Characterise current behaviour through real WordPress before any behaviour change. See the test list in the plan's 'Tests (Phase 2, extended in Phases 3 and 4)' section. The base TestCase also sets the admin screen for every test, because core admin_enqueue_scripts callbacks fatal without one.
findings: Only 1 of 8 integration tests drives WordPress admin state (test_wordpress_admin_menu_integration), and it only asserts $submenu is non-empty.

Fake or vacuous: test_capabilities_check_for_settings_access (asserts core current_user_can only), test_admin_menu_hook_registration (admin_menu already has callbacks without the hub; comment about the constructor is false), test_plugin_callback_execution (calls the stored closure directly), test_tabs_navigation_with_multiple_plugins ($_GET['page'] is never read by src; active tab never asserted).

Unit tests also extend WP_UnitTestCase and need MySQL. Only test_enqueue_styles_on_silver_assist_page drives WP_Styles, and it asserts enqueued only (not src/ver); test_enqueue_styles_not_on_other_pages cannot fail because URL resolution returns '' without plugin_file.

Singleton reset is inconsistent (unit: tearDown, integration: setUp) and admin-menu globals ($menu, $submenu, $_wp_submenu_nopriv, ...) are never reset, so do_action('admin_menu') accumulates state across tests.
Coverage cannot be measured locally (no xdebug/pcov on the dev machine); CI has xdebug and uploads to Codecov with fail_ci_if_error: false and no threshold.

tasks.notes: 48-phase-2-integration-tests, created with plain git (no gh issue develop link, so merging does not close #48).

tests/TestCase.php: resets the admin-menu globals and the style queue, resets the hub in setUp and tearDown, and offers login_as(), fire_admin_menu(), render(), render_registered_page(), can_access_page(), make_vendor_fixture() with cleanup, hub() and call_hub_method().
Unit setUp calls login_as(administrator).

Removed test_capabilities_check_for_settings_access, test_admin_menu_hook_registration, test_plugin_callback_execution and test_tabs_navigation_with_multiple_plugins; also the three render-only duplicates.

SettingsHubIntegrationTest (13 tests: menu tree, tab_title, registered callbacks, active tab, tabs off, access by role, no network admin hooks, priority 5) and the new StylesIntegrationTest (10 tests: handle, src, ver, hook wiring and suffixes, asset URL branches, plugin_file precedence).
Moved to the unit tier and extended: several plugins at once, Configure link, registration order.
Integration tests read $menu, $submenu, user_can_access_admin_page() or the callback WordPress registered; the render-only tests live in tests/Unit.
Deleted test_enqueue_styles_not_on_other_pages; test_enqueue_styles_on_silver_assist_page now uses make_vendor_fixture() and asserts src and ver.
Skipped: optional. Not needed yet; revisit if a test ever calls exit.
Not measurable locally (no xdebug or pcov). Read the percentage from the Codecov report of the Phase 2 PR for the log; the gate itself is Phase 6.

log.summary: Shared TestCase written; 24 existing tests and PHPStan still green. Remaining test work is split by file so it can be written in parallel worktrees: integration menu tests, integration styles tests, unit-tier tests.

Tests written in three parallel git worktrees by Sonnet subagents (menu integration, styles integration, unit tier) and merged by cherry-pick; the worktrees start at main, not at the phase branch, so each agent first reset its own empty branch to the phase tip. The unit track had to be re-run because its first agent stopped on a denied merge. Result: 53 tests (was 24), 250 assertions, green on WP 7.1.3 and with WP_MULTISITE=1, phpcs and phpstan clean, no test run twice.

Independent mutation check (scratch script, 20 hand-written mutants of src/SettingsHub.php applied one at a time to a throwaway copy): the old suite killed 6 of 20, the new suite kills 20 of 20. The mutants cover menu registration, capability, page callback, active tab, hook priority, menu position, enqueue, version, hook-suffix guard, asset path, escaping, action hook, plugin_file handling, empty label, button id, tabs flag and tab title.
Merged as PR #53 (squash, admin override because the only blocker was the required review) at 31e4f85. All 8 checks were green; #48 stayed open because the PR was not linked through gh issue develop.

workItems.title: Phase 3: Per-plugin capability
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-3-capability. Implement then document. Design decisions (correct here if the owner disagrees): parent menu and Dashboard stay manage_options, filterable via silverassist_settings_hub_dashboard_capability; per-plugin filter silverassist_settings_hub_plugin_capability; invalid values fail closed to manage_options with _doing_it_wrong; validation regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ (no sanitize_key, it lowercases); cards and tabs filtered with current_user_can; Dashboard tab hidden without the dashboard capability; wp_die(403) guard in render_plugin_page; capability assigned after array_merge. The Phase 2 access tests (test_administrator_can_access_every_hub_page, test_editor_and_subscriber_cannot_access_hub_pages) carry comments saying Phase 3 extends them; replace the editor/subscriber expectations as the capability work lands.
findings: src/SettingsHub.php:295, :307 and :322 hardcode manage_options; register_plugin() never reads $args['capability'].
IMPLEMENTATION.md:169, :250-280 and :1165 call the argument required since v1.1.1 and blame 403 errors on omitting it; that is false.
silver-assist-security/src/Admin/AdminPanel.php:262 passes 'capability' => 'manage_options' and requires the hub at ^1.2, so 1.3.0 is picked up without a constraint change.

WP core (7.1.3): add_submenu_page drops rows for users without the capability (plugin.php:1504-1507); user_can_access_admin_page checks the submenu's own capability (plugin.php:2234-2240); the top-level item stays and links to the first accessible submenu (menu.php:175-200, menu-header.php:157-173). Probe: editor reaches an edit_posts page under a manage_options parent, gets 403 on page=silver-assist.
options.php is gated by option_page_capability_{group} (options.php:29, :47); plugins lowering their capability and saving through the Settings API must filter it. Document it.
Existing unit render tests run as user 0 and will fail once cards are filtered per user; Phase 2 logs in an administrator first.

tasks.notes: 48-phase-3-capability, a plain branch from main (no gh issue develop link).

DEFAULT_CAPABILITY, normalize_capability() (regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$, trim, fail closed with _doing_it_wrong), get_plugin_capability(), get_dashboard_capability(), get_visible_plugins(). The capability is assigned after array_merge.

Parent menu and Dashboard use the dashboard capability; submenus use the plugin capability; cards and tabs use the visible plugins; the Dashboard tab needs the dashboard capability; render_plugin_page() ends in a 403 without the capability.
tests/Unit/CapabilityTest.php, 25 tests (a new file, to keep clear of the #49 branch that edits SettingsHubTest.php).

tests/Integration/CapabilityIntegrationTest.php, 11 tests with real editor, subscriber and administrator users. The top-level-menu-kept-for-editor case was not tested: core drops it in wp-admin/menu.php, which a test run does not load.
README (argument, new section, filters, option_page_capability caveat), IMPLEMENTATION.md (requirements line, examples, Error 2 rewritten, best practice), integration-guide.php (optional line).
Added, Changed and Documentation entries under [Unreleased], including the direct-call behaviour change.
89 tests (was 53), green on WP 7.1.3 and with WP_MULTISITE=1; phpcs and phpstan clean; independent mutation check killed 16 of 16 capability mutants and the earlier set still holds.

log.summary: Capability implemented as designed: optional argument, two filters, per-plugin cards, tabs and pages, 403 guard, docs and changelog. Backward compatible: the 53 existing tests pass unchanged and a registration that passes capability manage_options builds an identical menu. phpstan.neon: setExpectedIncorrectUsage added to the existing ignore for WordPress test-suite methods (Phase 6 revisits the ignores).

Interaction with the open UX branch (#49, feature/49-ux-design-system): its dashboard count uses count( $this->plugins ), which after this phase should count only the visible plugins, and its tests edit tests/Unit/SettingsHubTest.php, which Phase 2 rewrote. Whichever branch merges second must reconcile both. Not touched here.
Merged as PR #54 (squash d4d5f58). manual-check-as-editor was not done in a real wp-admin; role behaviour is covered by CapabilityIntegrationTest against real WordPress.

workItems.title: Phase 4: Code hardening
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-4-hardening. Each fix lands with a test that is red before and green after; record the red run in the log.
findings: register_submenus() is not idempotent: firing admin_menu twice yields [silver-assist, early, early, late]. A plugin registered from admin_menu priority 10 gets no submenu in that request.

enqueue_styles() uses strpos($hook_suffix, 'silver-assist'), which also matches settings_page_silver-assist-security and toplevel_page_not-silver-assist-at-all; the first clause is redundant. Core derives the submenu prefix from sanitize_title() of the translated parent title.
__wakeup() is public and empty: unserialize(serialize($hub)) !== $hub.

Callback actions print raw output inside a <script> click listener with no event parameter, run at render time, can collide on button id (sanitize_key of slug-label), and the code comment says AJAX although nothing is wired.
PACKAGE_VERSION is '1.2.0' at v1.2.2 and is the stylesheet ver; v1.2.1 changed the CSS.
assets/css/settings-hub.css:299-303 queries the container element itself (@container on .silverassist-dashboard-grid), which can never match.
Confirmed by a reproduction in Phase 2: registering from an admin_menu callback at priority 10 leaves the plugin out of $submenu in that request.

Slugs are not sanitised by register_plugin(): a slug containing < or > only survives escaping, and esc_url strips those characters from the Configure link, so the link no longer matches the registered page slug. Decide whether to sanitise the slug or document the allowed characters.

sanitize_key() strips spaces without a hyphen, so labels such as "Run Now" and "RunNow" on the same plugin produce the same button id (sa-action-<slug>-runnow); the unique-id work in this phase covers it.

The fallback success branch of get_package_asset_url() (package under ABSPATH) cannot be exercised in a test run, because the repository is never inside the WordPress install. Only its failure path is covered.

tasks.notes: PHPDoc of register_plugin() states the supported window. The long-form text is Phase 5 (IMPLEMENTATION.md, Registration timing).

Set PACKAGE_VERSION to 1.2.2 (newest released CHANGELOG heading). The test asserts equality with the first released ## [x.y.z] heading, skipping [Unreleased]. Phase 7 bumps to 1.3.0 together with the CHANGELOG move.
Already done by PR #51 (UX, #49), which removed the dead @container rule and the container-type declaration. A guard test (test_stylesheet_has_no_dead_container_query) keeps it from returning.

log.summary: Branch 48-phase-4-hardening created from main at e619288 with a plain git checkout -b (no gh issue develop link, which auto-closes #48 on merge).

Main moved while the phase was in progress: PR #51 (UX design system, #49) was merged (456f647). The branch was rebased onto it. #51 fixed the dead @container rule, but left the dashboard count at count( $this->plugins ), which after Phase 3 disagrees with the visible cards; fixed here with a test.

Red before green: with the new tests and the old src/ there were 11 failures out of 109 tests (idempotence, late registration x2, late-registration notice, no-notice window, hook-suffix look-alikes, translated parent title, unserialize, package version vs changelog, event parameter, unique button ids, visible count). After the change: 110 tests, 381 assertions, all green; composer phpcs and composer phpstan clean. Mutation check of the new behaviour: 14 of 14 mutants killed (scratchpad script mutation_p4.py).

Decisions: a registration after admin_menu has finished is still stored and its menu is built immediately, but it raises _doing_it_wrong() (core already built the menu). The hook suffix check reads the prefix core stored in $admin_page_hooks (falling back to sanitize_title of the translated title) instead of assuming English. Button ids keep the documented form for the first button and get -2, -3 for repeats within one dashboard render. Slug sanitisation was NOT added: a slug is a menu slug and WordPress itself accepts arbitrary strings; the allowed characters are documented in Phase 5 instead. Consumer risk to check in Phase 7: a consumer test suite that fires admin_menu and then registers a plugin now sees the notice (WP_UnitTestCase fails on unexpected _doing_it_wrong).

Merged as PR #59 (squash 928676b). Merged with admin override after all checks passed; the review requirement was the only blocker. The core-review pass was run late: the branch was pushed before it, and the pass was re-done manually over the changed docs and PR claims (no drift found), with 110 tests, phpcs and phpstan green on the branch before merge.

workItems.title: Phase 5a: Documentation that does not depend on Phase 3 or 4
workItems.notes: Branch 48-phase-5a-docs, stacked on 48-phase-3-capability. Split out of Phase 5 so it could be written in parallel with Phase 3. Written by a Sonnet subagent in a git worktree, then checked and corrected here; the three conflicts with the Phase 3 docs were small and were resolved by combining both sides. Once Phase 3 is merged, move this branch onto main with `git rebase --onto main 48-phase-3-capability 48-phase-5a-docs`.
findings: Part of the work was a decision, not a fix: the subagent removed the Packagist badges, the plain `composer require` and the "(private repository)" heading because the package and the standards repos are public and the package is on Packagist. The original install text was restored; the owner has to decide the install story (see questions in the PR).

The docs were checked against the code: PHPUnit 9.6, the CI jobs, composer scripts, the release workflow, plugin_file resolution, tabs default, tab_title and name semantics. Anchors and links resolve (0 problems) and the fences are balanced.
Merge conflicts with the Phase 3 docs appeared in README.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md and integration-guide.php, which is the cost of writing documentation in parallel with the code that changes it.

tasks.notes: Development pointer, PHPUnit 9.6, unsupported test claims removed, absolute links, broken anchor, version example, SVG icon wording, tabs default, tab_title/name/version semantics, plugin_file resolution, multisite sentence, undocumented CSS helper classes. Install story left as it was.
Rewritten: prerequisites, local setup, required test suite and MySQL, CI jobs, hooks, ruleset, commit convention, project layout, canonical release checklist.
43 lines, conventions and links only.
PHP 8.2+, embedded changelog and footer removed, generic WordPress advice trimmed, plugin_file in examples, ^1.2, no Packagist link.
plugin_file added; undocumented helper classes removed.
php -l, 0 broken links or anchors, balanced fences, no stale tool references.

log.summary: First attempt failed on a session limit before editing anything. Second attempt produced one commit; its report was checked against the code, the install-story change was reverted, a coverage-script description was softened and the Phase 3 conflicts were resolved.
Merged as PR #55 (squash e619288), rebased onto main after #54.

workItems.title: Phase 5: Documentation realignment
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-5-docs. Apply the canonical-home table and the correction list in the plan. Leave historical CHANGELOG entries alone. Review with core-review --budget thorough until it reports nothing new. Additional owners from the plan verification: README absolute links (release zip lacks IMPLEMENTATION.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and integration-guide.php), README Development pointer, PHPUnit 9.6, action contract, tab_title/name/version semantics, multisite scope; IMPLEMENTATION.md Registration timing, plugin_file in examples, ^1.2, one update-button example; CONTRIBUTING layout, skip-db-create, composer test vs phpunit, spelling; .packagist.yml; SettingsHub.php docblock wording. Phase 5a (a separate work item) already did the behaviour-independent documentation; what remains here is the documentation of Phase 4 behaviour (registration window, hook suffixes, action-button contract, hooks and filters table), the README install-story decision, the composer.json wording, the slevomat dependency, the text-domain statement and .packagist.yml.
findings: IMPLEMENTATION.md requires PHP 8.3+ (:40, :95, :1147) while composer.json requires ^8.2; it embeds a stale changelog and version footer (:1322-1344) and claims built-in update support (:33).
'Settings > Silver Assist' in composer.json:3, the class docblock and copilot-instructions.md contradicts the top-level menu at position 80.

CONTRIBUTING.md and copilot-instructions.md describe a Brain Monkey fallback; README.md:19 and copilot-instructions.md:17,46 say PHPUnit 10 (the repo uses PHPUnit 9.6); the bootstrap hard-requires the WP test suite.
README Development section is duplicated (:450-512 and :514-554) with a stray fence at :512 and wrong test counts; the anchor IMPLEMENTATION.md#integration-with-wp-github-updater does not exist.
Install docs mix Packagist badges and plain composer require with the private vcs-repository requirement; CONTRIBUTING omits the token needed for dev dependencies.
copilot-instructions.md documents a non-existent `composer phpcs:fix`, a stale file tree, add_options_page and the Settings API, and Slevomat (a dev dependency no ruleset uses).

Undocumented: tab_title also labels the sidebar submenu; plugin_file is first-wins and fails silently outside ABSPATH; the Dashboard hook suffix toplevel_page_silver-assist; the action callback signature; the silverassist-settings-hub text domain is never loaded.
IMPLEMENTATION.md:351 describes onclick attributes; the code uses an addEventListener <script> block.

The register_plugin() docblock says plugin_file is taken from the "first plugin that registers"; the code keeps the first NON-EMPTY plugin_file (src/SettingsHub.php:140-142). Pinned by StylesIntegrationTest::test_first_non_empty_plugin_file_wins_when_earlier_registrations_have_none.

tasks.notes: Verify (do not rewrite) the Error 2 section that Phase 3 writes.
Waiting for the owner decision on the install story (Packagist, vcs with token, or both). README install section and .packagist.yml were deliberately not touched.
Class docblock "Settings > Silver Assist" and the PHPDoc at src/SettingsHub.php:179-180.

log.summary: Executed by three Sonnet agents in isolated worktrees (docs, meta, phpstan) with two independent review lenses per track and up to three revise rounds. Docs track: 4 + 2 fix commits after two rounds with actionable findings (false claim that a second registration of a slug replaces the submenu, wrong claim that priority 4 is the only one working before 1.3.0, slug URL characters, return value of add_menu_page). Meta track: no actionable findings. slevomat/coding-standard was removed only as a direct dev dependency: it stays installed because silverassist/wp-coding-standards requires it, and the phpcs result is unchanged. The orchestrator merged the tracks into 48-phase-5-docs, softened the claim about admin_menu priority 5 itself (depends on callback order) and made the JS names in IMPLEMENTATION.md consistent. Not done on purpose: packagist-yml-and-contributing-details (install story pending), consolidating the update button material into one example (only the names were unified), and stating the registration window only in IMPLEMENTATION.md (the README and integration guide repeat it briefly). Verified on the branch: 110 tests, phpcs and phpstan green, composer validate --strict ok, php -l on integration-guide.php.
Merged as PR #62 (squash 5e42121) with admin override. Item stays in-progress only because packagist-yml-and-contributing-details is blocked on the install story decision.

workItems.title: Phase 6: PHPStan tightening
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-6-phpstan. Keep src/ fully clean; a tests/-only baseline is acceptable for the 2.x upgrade if logged as a follow-up.
findings: With reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors: true, three ignore patterns are stale (Undefined type \WP_UnitTestCase, Use of unknown class \WP_UnitTestCase, Class .* extends unknown class WP_UnitTestCase).

With the ignoreErrors list removed: 106 errors (13 in src/SettingsHub.php, 33 in tests/Integration, 59 in tests/Unit, 1 in tests/bootstrap.php). src errors are array-shape casts (:141, :148, :384, :386, :398, :406, ...) and Constant ABSPATH not found (:267).
phpstan/phpstan is on 1.12.x (^1.10); szepeviktor/phpstan-wordpress already allows ^2.0.
The first ignore in phpstan.neon, `Right side of && is always true`, is still matched by src/SettingsHub.php:464 and must be deleted for the stated end state to hold.

workItems.title: Phase 7: Release 1.3.0 and consumer verification
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-7-release-1-3-0. Tags are immutable; never move or delete an existing tag. Order matters: the consumer verification runs before the tag.
findings: CHANGELOG.md lacks a [1.2.2] compare link and [Unreleased] still compares from v1.2.1.
The only consumer is silver-assist-security (requires ^1.2 via a vcs repository); its own SettingsHub integration test only checks that the hub resolves.

tasks.notes: Branch 48-phase-7-release created from main at 03386b5 (after the release tooling PR #60, squash 03386b5).

Prepared with scripts/update-version.sh 1.3.0 --date 2026-10-15: [Unreleased] became [1.3.0], links added. The date is the preparation date, change the heading date if the tag is pushed on another day. Reworded the PACKAGE_VERSION entry so it stays true after the bump.
PACKAGE_VERSION is 1.3.0 in the same commit; scripts/check-versions.sh --expect 1.3.0 passes.

Done on a copy of silver-assist-security (the working repo was not touched), hub swapped to 1.3.0 through a composer path repository with a forced 1.3.0 version, own WordPress test library and database. Full PHPUnit suite with WPGraphQL and Contact Form 7 installed so the admin page tests run: 889 tests, 3920 assertions, 0 failures, 5 skipped (multisite, CF7 stub), identical to the same run with the hub 1.2.x it currently locks. No _doing_it_wrong notice from the late registration check.
